facts.statement: A restricted-license driver aged 15 may travel for a job, employment or farm work.
A restricted-license driver aged 15 may take the direct home-school route on school days for attendance, excluding school activities.
A restricted-license driver aged 15 may travel directly to or from an activity held by a religious organization.
A restricted-license driver aged 15 may drive when a licensed adult sits in front.
Restricted-license drivers aged 15 may not carry minors who are not siblings.
A restricted-license driver may use a wireless device only for reporting unlawful activity or summoning emergency help.
A restricted-license driver aged 16 may drive between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m.
A restricted-license driver aged 16 may travel to or from school and authorized school activities.
A restricted-license driver aged 16 may travel directly to or from a religious organization's activity.
A restricted-license driver aged 16 may drive for work, employment or farm duties.
A restricted-license driver aged 16 may drive while accompanied by a licensed adult in front.
A restricted-license driver aged 16 may carry only one minor passenger who is not a sibling.
After reaching age 16 and holding a restricted license for 6 months, the driver is released from all age-related driving restrictions described in the handbook.
Applicants younger than 18 seeking an unrestricted license need a parent or guardian affidavit confirming at least 50 practice hours.
The unrestricted-license practice affidavit for applicants below 18 must include at least 10 nighttime hours.
An unrestricted-license applicant must pass vision, written and driving exams or present the gold DE-99 driver-education completion slip.
A license applicant may take station vision screening or present the Driver Licensing eye-examination form completed within the previous 90 days by a licensed ophthalmologist or optometrist.
Station vision screening requires at least 20/40 vision in one eye.
Drivers who need corrective lenses to meet the vision standard receive a restriction requiring those lenses whenever driving.
An applicant who fails vision screening must have the licensing eye form completed by a licensed ophthalmologist or optometrist.
Returning the eye form within 90 days of examination lets licensing staff decide whether to issue a license or require further testing.
The Kansas knowledge exam covers traffic law and sign recognition by shape, color or symbol.
The driving exam uses a designated traffic route to demonstrate basic vehicle-operation skills.
Graduated licensing introduces beginner drivers to more complex situations in stages after initial lower-risk experience.
After the first, second or third failure of the written or driving exam, next-working-day retesting is available after payment of the re-exam fee.
The handbook lists a re-examination fee of one dollar and fifty cents.
Applicants receive four opportunities to pass the written exam.
Applicants receive four opportunities to pass the driving exam.
A fourth failure of either exam requires waiting at least 6 months from the latest failure before retesting.
An applicant receives a license only after passing the required exams and meeting the other licensing conditions.
Renewing an instructional permit requires passing the written exam again.
A temporary resident's license, permit or identification card expires when lawful-presence authorization expires.
The Division sends a license-expiration or renewal notice at least 30 days before expiration.
Renewal notices use the mailing address on record or the email address selected for electronic notices.
For renewal, a licensed ophthalmologist's or optometrist's eye examination may replace station screening if completed no more than 90 days before the renewal application.
A licensing examiner may require a renewal applicant to take a written or driving test when ordinary vehicle control is in doubt.
The handbook lists an additional expired-license penalty of one dollar.
A license expired for more than one year requires vision, written and driving testing.
A Kansas license may generally be renewed at any state driver-license office regardless of the holder's Kansas residence.
Registered offenders must use a full-service station for renewal.
A separate-card concealed-carry license holder may renew at any station if no name, address or license-number changes are needed.
Three moving-violation convictions within 12 months can cause a license suspension.
For a first chemical-test refusal, the handbook requires a one-year suspension.
For a second chemical-test refusal, the handbook requires a two-year suspension.
For a third chemical-test refusal, the handbook requires a three-year suspension.
For a fourth chemical-test refusal, the handbook requires a ten-year suspension.
Failure to appear for a required court date carries an indefinite suspension under the handbook.
Failure to respond to a traffic citation from Kansas or another state can cause license suspension.
Failure to keep continuous vehicle liability insurance carries an indefinite suspension.
Impaired driving or an alcohol-test result of.08 or higher can cause suspension.
Transporting an open alcoholic-beverage container can cause suspension.
Failure to report a traffic crash can cause suspension.
A vehicular-homicide conviction can result in revoked driving privileges.
A conviction for leaving a crash involving injury or death without stopping and helping can cause revocation.
A reckless-driving conviction can cause revocation.
A conviction for a felony committed using a motor vehicle can result in license revocation.
A conviction for trying to evade a police officer can cause revocation.
An aggravated-vehicular-homicide conviction can result in license revocation.
A vehicular-battery conviction can result in license revocation.
A student who lives outside Kansas and is classified as nonresident for tuition purposes may drive on a valid license in Kansas from age 16.
Active-duty military members and qualifying spouses and children may drive on a valid license in Kansas from age 16.
An employee aged 16 or older of a company licensed to do business in Kansas may use a valid license while temporarily employed in Kansas to receive or provide job instruction.
Foreign tourists, teachers and business visitors staying up to one year may use a valid license from age 16 with valid immigration documents.
A nonresident visitor with a valid state license may drive in Kansas from age 16.
Information on a renewal eye-examination form may lead to additional testing.
Foreign military personnel temporarily serving with the Armed Forces, and their spouses or children, may drive on a valid license in Kansas from age 16.
A Class C license permits a vehicle whose gross vehicle weight rating is below 26,001 pounds.
The handbook says a driver's license expires on the holder's birthday.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: A restricted-license driver aged 16 may drive for school and approved school activities.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: A restricted-license driver aged 16 may travel to or from school and authorized school activities.
changed_existing_facts.issue: For school does not retain the to/from limitation.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: After reaching 16 and holding a restricted license for 6 months, the listed age restrictions end.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: After reaching age 16 and holding a restricted license for 6 months, the driver is released from all age-related driving restrictions described in the handbook.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Listed restrictions relies on absent surrounding material rather than naming the age-related restrictions.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: An unrestricted-license applicant must pass vision, written and driving tests or supply the specified driver-education completion slip.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: An unrestricted-license applicant must pass vision, written and driving exams or present the gold DE-99 driver-education completion slip.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Specified completion slip is not self-contained; source specifies the gold DE-99 slip.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: License applicants undergo station vision screening or submit an eye-examination form completed by a licensed eye specialist within 90 days.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: A license applicant may take station vision screening or present the Driver Licensing eye-examination form completed within the previous 90 days by a licensed ophthalmologist or optometrist.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Licensed eye specialist is broader than the two professions named; the source also specifies the Driver Licensing form and previous ninety days.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: After a failed written or driving exam, retesting is available on the next working day after payment of the re-exam fee.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: After the first, second or third failure of the written or driving exam, next-working-day retesting is available after payment of the re-exam fee.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The standalone retest rule omits the fourth-failure waiting exception, which is not optional even though separately recorded in R29.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Renewal includes vision screening, with a qualifying eye-specialist examination from within 90 days accepted instead.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: For renewal, a licensed ophthalmologist's or optometrist's eye examination may replace station screening if completed no more than 90 days before the renewal application.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Within ninety days has no reference date, and qualifying eye specialist omits the named professions.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: The handbook lists chemical-test refusal suspensions of one year for a first refusal, two for a second, three for a third and ten for a fourth.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: For a first chemical-test refusal, the handbook requires a one-year suspension.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Values match, but four separately testable claims violate one-claim fact granularity; each proposed sentence must be a separate fact.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Failing to attend a required court date or respond to a traffic citation can produce an indefinite suspension.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: Failure to appear for a required court date carries an indefinite suspension under the handbook.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The paraphrase applies the indefinite duration to the separate citation-response alternative, which the page does not explicitly do. Split the two proposed sentences into separate facts.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Using a vehicle to commit a felony can result in license revocation.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: A conviction for a felony committed using a motor vehicle can result in license revocation.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The source conditions revocation on conviction; the standalone statement omits that condition.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Aggravated vehicular homicide can cause license revocation.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: An aggravated-vehicular-homicide conviction can result in license revocation.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The standalone statement omits the conviction condition.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Vehicular battery can cause license revocation.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: A vehicular-battery conviction can result in license revocation.
changed_existing_facts.issue: The standalone statement omits the conviction condition.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Nonresident students with a valid license may drive in Kansas if they are at least 16.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: A student who lives outside Kansas and is classified as nonresident for tuition purposes may drive on a valid license in Kansas from age 16.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Living out of state and classification as nonresident for tuition purposes were reduced to generic nonresidency.

changed_existing_facts.original_statement: Temporarily assigned qualifying company trainees or instructors may drive on a valid license in Kansas from age 16.
changed_existing_facts.corrected_statement: An employee aged 16 or older of a company licensed to do business in Kansas may use a valid license while temporarily employed in Kansas to receive or provide job instruction.
changed_existing_facts.issue: Qualifying company is not self-contained; Kansas business licensing and temporary employment for job instruction are missing.

unverifiable_dispositions.original_statement: The handbook states that a fifth alcohol-test result of.08 or higher or chemical-test refusal leads to permanent revocation.

debts.text: Withheld assertion sec01-R56: The handbook states that a fifth alcohol-test result of.08 or higher or chemical-test refusal leads to permanent revocation. Reason: The source's fifth-result/refusal syntax is ambiguous about how the ordinal applies to refusal. The standalone wording can imply permanent revocation for any refusal, conflicting with earlier refusal tiers. Current-law interpretation is outside this review. The original meaning, quantity and source page are retained here as unresolved debt; it is not a learner fact.
